free_tier.stated: Free, unlimited distribution; ~1.4 million items already torrented, 'comprising almost a petabyte of public domain materials'. Egress is unbounded because the swarm and webseeds share the load.

egress.terms: Torrents rely heavily on webseeding: download directly from Archive servers when no peers have the files. The page states no price and no bandwidth limit for torrent or webseed download.

record.interface_detail: BitTorrent protocol: .torrent files per item with Getright-style webseeding, tracked by bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org
record.tooling: A BitTorrent client with Getright-style webseeding support; the Archive generates the .torrent per item and runs the trackers bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org.
record.chaining: Archive BitTorrents are made automatically for community-contributed items in many collections and updated when the item changes. The torrent falls back on webseeding from Archive servers when no peers have the files.
record.limits_note: Torrents become obsolete when the item changes, and some or all files then fail to download completely. Clients without Getright-style webseeding, such as rTorrent, cannot download un-seeded Archive torrents. The ._____padding_file directory should be deselected. The trackers bt1.archive.org and bt2.archive.org are closed and track only the Archive's own torrents. A torrent for an item without one is requested by email to info@archive.org.

identity_cost.detail: The torrent page names no account requirement for downloading. Creating the item that receives an Archive torrent needs a free archive.org account.

record.reliability_note: Old torrents for a mutated item loop forever re-downloading mismatched pieces; seeder counts are cached ~5 minutes and include webseeds.
